title: TypeScript SDK: 'stream-morph' adapter for resumable AsyncIterator <-> ReadableStream interop
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our TypeScript SDK exposes both AsyncIterator and Web ReadableStream shapes but lacks a single ergonomic bridge that preserves cancellation semantics, backpressure, and enables resumable consumption across network retries or transient failures. Current examples scatter helper functions and produce inconsistent behavior when callers attempt to checkpoint/resume or when SDK-level retries re-invoke the request.

Goal: Implement a 'stream-morph' adapter primitive that: (1) wraps a single underlying transport stream and exposes safe, well-typed conversions to AsyncIterator and ReadableStream; (2) preserves source backpressure so the serving runtime and clients see expected latency/cost tradeoffs; (3) supports checkpointing tokens for resumable consumption (useful for reconnects and retry-with-resume scenarios); (4) integrates with SDK retry policies so that a retry can optionally resume from the last checkpoint instead of restarting from the beginning; (5) has clear TypeScript types and small ergonomic surface for users (factory + methods).

Why unique: Many existing tickets cover conversion or ergonomic patterns for streaming but this ticket focuses on a single reusable primitive that intentionally exposes a resume protocol + well-defined cancellation propagation across both shapes and ties into the SDK retry layer. It also includes a small example app and a migration recipe for customers currently using DIY helpers.
acceptance_criteria:
- Exported API: createStreamMorph(options) documented with types and examples.
- Methods available: toAsyncIterator(), toReadableStream(), checkpoint() -> string, resume(checkpointToken) -> restores iterator/stream at last checkpoint.
- Cancellation initiated from either consumer shape (iterator.return() or ReadableStream cancel()) triggers underlying connection abort and releases resources.
- SDK retry policy has a new enum value 'resume-on-retry' that, when enabled, calls resume(checkpoint) and only falls back to full retry if resume fails.
- Unit tests cover conversions, cancellation propagation, single-producer multi-consumer safety, and resume semantics.
- Integration tests simulate transient network failure and verify resume-on-retry avoids re-streaming first N tokens.
- Performance benchmark added: compare baseline (no morph adapter) vs morph adapter for 1k concurrent short-lived streams, with percentiles and token cost impact.
- Docs: Console streaming guide updated, and a short migration guide included in the SDK changelog/README.
design_notes:
High-level design: a StreamMorph object will own the transport ReadableStream (underlying native stream from fetch/WebSocket/etc.). It will maintain an internal small ring buffer of last N bytes/frames and expose periodic checkpoint markers (opaque strings) representing a stable point in the consumption. Checkpoint semantics are advisory: we will only guarantee resume if the server supports server-side offsets or if the cached KV cache has the prefix available.

Components:
- TransportLayer: thin abstraction over fetch ReadableStream / WebSocket stream that exposes pull/push, current offset, and a low-level cancel() API.
- BufferWindow: configurable sliding window (default 64KB / 128 tokens) used to produce checkpoint tokens and to rehydrate resumed consumers without a full restart when server doesn't support offset resume.
- StreamMorph API: createStreamMorph({transport, tokenWindowBytes, checkpointIntervalMs}) -> StreamMorph instance with toAsyncIterator(), toReadableStream(), checkpoint(), resume().

Types & ergonomics:
- Use generics: StreamMorph<T> where T is the parsed chunk type (string | Token | StructuredChunk).
- Keep examples short: const morph = createStreamMorph(transport); for await (const c of morph.toAsyncIterator()) {} 

Retry integration:
- Add resume-aware hook in sdk/retries.ts: onRetry(context) -> if context.resumeTokens present && policy === 'resume-on-retry' then attempt morph.resume(token). If resume succeeds, continue; else fallback to full retry.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strong guarantee vs practicality: full server-side offset resume is ideal but many models/servers don't support it. We'll provide best-effort resume using client-side window buffer and explicit server capabilities metadata.
- Memory: window increases memory usage per stream; default is small and tunable.
- Complexity: API includes checkpoint primitives which adds surface area; mitigated by simple defaults and examples.
implementation_plan:
1) RFC PR: add design diagram + sequence diagrams to docs (confluence link). 2) Implement core StreamMorph in packages/ts-sdk/src/stream-morph.ts with feature-flag gate. 3) Add integration with existing fetch-based streaming transport (packages/ts-sdk/src/transport/fetch-stream.ts). 4) Add unit tests in packages/ts-sdk/test/stream-morph.test.ts covering conversions, cancellation, checkpoint/resume. 5) Add end-to-end scenario test using the local stream emulator service (test-fixtures/stream-emulator). 6) Instrument metrics: morph.active_count, morph.resume_attempts, morph.resume_success_rate. 7) Docs: add example in docs/streaming.md and a migration snippet for existing customers. 8) Ship behind feature flag and enable for 10% of beta customers.

Milestones & PRs:
- Draft RFC: https://confluence.company/TS-SDK-Stream-Morph (placeholder)
- Implementation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ts-sdk/pull/### (will update)
- E2E test harness updates: https://github.com/redwood-inference/stream-fixtures/pull/###
test_plan:
Unit tests:
- Conversion tests: validate the same chunk sequence is produced by both toAsyncIterator() and toReadableStream() when consumed sequentially.
- Cancellation tests: calling iterator.return() must abort the transport and cause stream.cancel() consumers to receive a DOMException-like abort.
- Checkpoint/resume tests: simulate server that can accept an offset resume and one that cannot. Validate morph.resume(token) yields same subsequent chunks or errors with clear message.

Integration tests:
- Simulate transient TCP drop mid-stream, trigger SDK retry with policy 'resume-on-retry' and verify resumed consumer only receives post-checkpoint chunks and token cost is reduced.
- Load test: 1k concurrent short-lived streams. Measure 95/99 latency and memory increase per worker.

Observability tests:
- Ensure morph metrics appear in telemetry and dashboards. Add smoke alert if resume_success_rate < 95% for beta customers.
performance_considerations:
- Backpressure: ensure ReadableStream backpressure is honored by transporting pull-based reads to the engine to avoid over-fetching tokens (reduce cost).
- Overhead: BufferWindow introduces copy/retain cost. Keep defaults small and document trade-offs.
- CPU: parsing/resuming may add CPU; measure in CI microbenchmarks and add a tunable 'checkpointIntervalMs' to trade CPU vs resume granularity.
- Memory: default window 64KB; monitor heap per stream in load test.
comments: 2026-02-21 - Aisha Patel: Pitched the idea in eng-all. Positive feedback from SDK and Runtime. Next: spike a PoC buffer-window implementation.

2026-02-28 - Diego Chen: Completed PoC that converts a fetch ReadableStream to AsyncIterator with a 32KB sliding window. Found an edge-case where double-consume can occur if both shapes are active simultaneously. Plan to prevent multi-active consumers by gating with an acquisition token.

2026-03-03 - Samira Khan (runtime): Ran PoC under 200 concurrent streams. Observed 6% increase in p95 latency when window set to 256KB; recommending default 64KB and a warning in docs for larger windows.

2026-03-08 - Diego Chen: Implemented checkpoint token format (base64 JSON: {version, offset, crc}). Added resume fallback to full restart when server doesn't advertise resume capability. PR drafted for review.
2026-03-10 - PM review (Lena Ortiz): Approved feature gate approach. Requested adding a small migration note in console docs and adding customer feature-flagging controls for Private deployments.

2026-03-12 - Security (R. Mills): Reviewed abort semantics and confirmed no new sensitive data is stored in buffer windows. Requested explicit opt-in for longer windows in Private deployments (compliance).
